newsitem.title: UK: B.A.T interested in buying life insurer.
newsitem.headline: B.A.T interested in buying life insurer.

text.p: B.A.T Industries Plc said on Wednesday it was interested in expanding its operations in the UK life insurance sector through acquisition but had been put off bidding for mutual insurer Scottish Amicable because of the price.
B.A.T, which has extensive tobacco interests, already owns insurance businesses Allied Dunbar and Eagle Star in Britain and Farmers in the U.S.

"We've said in the past that the portfolio of brands in our British American Financial Services unit would benefit from filling out in the life broker business," said B.A.T chief executive Martin Broughton.
"Too many people were looking at Scottish Amicable, I think it would have turned out to be too high a price."
Scottish Amicable effectively put itself up for sale in February and is considering bids from Prudential Corp, Abbey National and Australian Mutual Provident.

Broughton's remarks echoed comments made at the halfway stage that the group wanted to build its presence in the independent financial advice (IFA) segment, which accounts for around half of all UK life insurance and pension business.
But B.A.T chairman Lord Cairns refused to comment on speculation suggesting that the group had approached Commercial Union as a possible partner for its financial services business.
He did say the company remained open-minded about its future structure, leaving the door open to a possible demerger.
"We are not wedded to a particular structure... We have an open mind," said Cairns.
